thresholdRule.statement: Every bound of this file is inherited from a committed bound of thresholds.json by one rule: a new leg that measures the same quantity as a Part A leg, on other statements or other draws, carries that leg's committed bound unchanged. No bound is chosen here.
thresholdRule.D8b: D8b measures the quantity of C3.coverageU3 (U3, coverage at 0.95 of the reported statement, a zero-estimate bin covered when the truth is below its upper limit) restricted to the bins where zero estimates occur, so its pooled coverage carries C3's committed interval [0.90, 0.99], in the prototype and in the oracle. Its lowest single bin may not fall below the lower edge of that interval, 0.90, which is also C4b's committed bound for a lowest single bin. D8's own figure (>= 0.94) was the bound of a different, conditional quantity and is not inherited; whether the pooled unconditional coverage also reaches 0.94 is reported without a status.
thresholdRule.penalty: The share of penalised fits that do not meet the stopping rule carries C6's committed bound on the share of fits that do not converge (<= 0.005). Agreement of a penalised estimate with the oracle carries P2's tolerance (tolerance.penaltyOracle, 1e-4 in ln Gamma). The benefit of the penalty carries P3's bound (<= 0.9). Two routes of the prototype that must give one answer carry tolerance.continuity (1e-5). The oracle's own two algorithms must agree two decades inside the tolerance they certify (1e-6 in theta), the same ratio as O1 keeps to R2 (1e-8 held to far better than the 1e-8 it certifies is not available as a rule, so the ratio is stated here and fixed before any run).
thresholdRule.authentic: X1 and X2 keep the bounds thresholds.json gave them ('inside the published table's own uncertainty, set by the request's data'; 'set by the request's data'). What that is for the files actually fetched is fixed by an amendment recorded after the fetch and before any estimate from those files is computed by any program (decision F-DEC6).
thresholdRule.exact: A reproduction of a pinned Part A number is exact for integers and to tolerance.closedForm (1e-12, relative) for floating-point numbers.

measurement.statement: As AM1 (2) of thresholds.json, unchanged: the reported statement of a bin is covered when its status is ok and D_j(Gamma_true) is at or below the chi-square threshold of 0.95 (one constrained fit at the truth); when its status is upper-limit and Gamma_true is at or below the limit (a null limit covers); a status not-constrained, refused or not converged does not cover. The zero rule is tested on the fit: mu_hat_j below 1e-6.
measurement.d8b: coverage = covered statements / all statements of the bins of Z over every replicate, whatever the estimate (the unconditional measurement). perBin = the same for each bin of Z. The conditional share (D8's quantity: covered / zero-estimate statements) is reported beside it and judged by nothing.
measurement.stoppingRule: A penalised fit 'meets the stopping rule' when the fit's own converged flag is true under the rule in force (the default of 48d21711 in the diagnostic and in F3; the repaired rule in PC1 to PC4).
measurement.diagnostic: For every penalised fit of Part A's sets the validator records, through a diagnostic return that changes no arithmetic: the converged flag, the iterations, why the loop ended (criterion, no accepted step in 40 tries, or the cap of 1000), the final damping, the final largest absolute gradient component g, g divided by the number of listings, the Newton decrement d = (1/2) g' H^-1 g at the final point (the objective's expected fall from one more step), the rounding floor f = 16 x 2^-52 x max(1, |objective|), the smallest eigenvalue of the final Hessian, and the largest absolute difference of theta from the oracle's optimum on the same sample.
measurement.classification: A fit that does not meet the default rule is 'at the optimum' iff its theta is within 1e-6 of the oracle's optimum in every bin (the PO1 tolerance), and then 'rounding floor' iff d <= f, otherwise 'stalled above the floor'; it is 'not at the optimum' otherwise. The class counts are reported rows; they decide which kind of repair the amendment may make (repairLimits) and nothing else.
measurement.repairLimits: The repaired stopping rule, to be recorded as an amendment after the diagnostic's rows are pinned and before the first run of any fit under it: (1) is scale-free, i.e. stated relative to the number of listings or to the objective, as the gate document's recorded recommendation ('a criterion relative to the count'); (2) states every constant; (3) if every non-converged fit of the diagnostic is 'at the optimum', changes only when the iteration stops and what the converged flag says, never the objective, the start, the step or the damping; if some are 'stalled above the floor' it may also change the damping and says so; if any is 'not at the optimum' no repair is attempted in this follow-up and PC1 to PC4 fail as unmeasurable; (4) is an option of the penalised fit that is off by default, so that Part A's stream is reproducible (F3); (5) is judged on P3c and P4c, whose seeds no run has used when it is written.
measurement.penaltyAgreement: max over bins of |theta_prototype - theta_oracle| (theta = ln Gamma), every fit counted whether or not its flag says converged.
measurement.p3: As P3.penaltyHelps and AM1 (6): the mean over replicates of the sum over the ten bins of (Gamma_hat / Gamma - 1)^2 at kappa 4 divided by the same for the unpenalised fit; a replicate in which either fit does not meet its stopping rule is dropped from both and counted.
measurement.crossFeedAgreement: For D8b.r2: on each of the oracle's U3c samples and each bin of Z, the prototype's status and covering flag against the oracle's; a statement whose oracle deviance at the truth lies within 1e-6 of the threshold, or whose oracle limit lies within 1e-9 (relative) of the truth, is exempt from the flag comparison and counted.

amendments.recordedBefore: the follow-up oracle's first run (no follow-up program had been run and no sample drawn)
amendments.text: Definitions the contract left open, fixed before any number exists; no bound moved. (1) 'The oracle's optimum' of a penalised fit, wherever a leg or a diagnostic compares with it, is the result of the oracle's Newton iteration (flat start; a full step once the step is below 1e-7, backtracking on the objective above that; stopped when the largest step component is below 1e-12 or at 400 iterations; a Hessian whose smallest eigenvalue is not positive is shifted for the step). Part A's BFGS result is the second algorithm and PO1 bounds the distance between the two; F2 compares the BFGS result with Part A's pinned theta, which BFGS produced. (2) Per-sample output stays outside the repository beside the sample files, regenerable by seed: the oracle's U3c samples and its statement table (status, covering flag, the deviance at the truth or the limit, for the bins of Z), the stream sample files, and the oracle's penalised theta of every stream fit. A commit pins each file by its sha256 together with the counts the legs read; the validator checks every sha256 before it compares. Sample files hold every double in its shortest round-trip decimal form, so both implementations read identical numbers; the 12-digit rounding of Part A's reference samples is not applied to the follow-up's ensembles. (3) 'Copied without change' is measured as the source text of each copied function being found verbatim in tools/population-oracle/oracle.py, whose sha256 is recorded. (4) In the oracle's U3c ensemble a constrained fit or a limit is computed only for the bins of Z; for the other bins only the zero rule's status is recorded (for the count of zero estimates outside Z). (5) A sample with no object has no penalised fit in either implementation; it is counted and belongs to no leg. (6) The exact counts-path coverage of D8b.r3 sums the Poisson distribution over counts 0 to 399. (7) F2's log-likelihood comparison is made once per reference sample and kappa with the copied fit_lbfgs, which is the fit that produced the pinned value.

amendments.recordedBefore: the oracle's stage 2b and every validator run; recorded AFTER the oracle's stages 1 and 2, which it does not change
amendments.text: What the oracle's second stage did not read, and one plain statement about it. (1) PD3 asks for the class counts of Part A's P4 ensemble (seeds 264850 to 265249), and a class needs the oracle's optimum on the same sample; stage 2 read P3, P3c and P4c only. The sample writer gains the set P4 and the oracle a stage 2b that reads that one file and adds its own block and its own theta file, leaving the blocks and files of stages 1 and 2 as pinned (checked by sha256). PD3 is a reported row; no judged leg reads stage 2b except PO1, whose statement covers every penalised fit the oracle makes. (2) Stage 2's output shows that the oracle's Newton iteration ended at its cap of 400 iterations in at least one fit of P3 and of P3c, with a largest remaining gradient component of 5.4e-8: its backtracking compares objectives, which is the stall the diagnostic is to test in the prototype. The oracle is not changed: PO1 judges it as it ran (its two algorithms agree to 1.6e-7 against the committed 1e-6), and the accuracy of 'the oracle's optimum' in the classification is therefore about 1e-7, inside the 1e-6 the classification uses. (3) The prototype's diagnostic return is requested by penalty.diagnostic = true and adds fields to the penalty record only; the smallest eigenvalue of the final Hessian is computed in the validator by Jacobi rotations. No bound moved.

decisions.text: D8b is judged on new draws. Part A's record already gives the unconditional coverage of the bins of Z on Part A's ensemble (0.94975), so a leg on that ensemble would be a bound committed after its result. The Part A ensemble is used for reproduction only.

D8b carries C3's interval and not D8's 0.94, by the rule of thresholdRule: it is C3's quantity on a subset of C3's bins, and Part A committed [0.90, 0.99] for a nominal 0.95 on sparse counts before any number existed. Whether 0.94 is reached is reported so that the reader can apply the stricter figure; Carl may rule that it should have been the bound, which would be a reset recorded as a new row.

The repaired stopping rule is fixed after the diagnostic and before its first run, inside limits committed here, and is judged on seeds no run has used. The alternative, committing a rule now from a reading of the code alone, would turn an undiagnosed guess into the thing judged, which is what the ruling's order (diagnose, then a new leg) avoids.
The diagnostic adds a return of intermediate quantities to the penalised fit and changes no arithmetic; F3 measures that by exact reproduction.

A passing D8b is recorded as 'A through D8b' because register row D-R10-264-02 and question 1 of the gate document name the follow-up leg as what would let the per-object-uncertainty set stand; it is a recommendation to Carl in a DELEGATED row and changes nothing that is built.

The authentic legs' contracts cannot be written before the files are seen, because thresholds.json left their bounds to the request's data. They are fixed by amendment after the fetch and before any program computes an estimate from the files. What may be looked at before that amendment: the files' documentation, column names, units and row counts, the paper's text and its published table (the comparison target, necessarily read). What may not: any rate, exposure or count computed from the files by the prototype, the oracle or by hand. The contract has no free parameter chosen by its agreement with the published table.
X3 stays NOT RUN whatever is fetched under R4 (ruling 4). R3's text is fetched and recorded for a later lesson and no leg of this follow-up reads it.

The cross-feed of D8b and the exact counts-path coverage are reported rows, not judged legs: the gate document defined D8b as one measurement and the oracle's own ensemble is the independent check the gate pattern asks for. They are recorded so that a disagreement, if any, is on the page.
